evidence: The focused eight-case blob and candidate-retention suite plus the complete 80-test workflow suite passed on the exact clean candidate.
Git arguments remain structured, diagnostics remain redacted, and candidate evidence reads stay inside verified repository objects.
PILOT-001-R4-001 violates the immutable RED evidence contract across a multi-round ticket.
PILOT-001-R4-002 shows that per-file limits do not bound aggregate Git bytes or subprocess count.
The shared validateGitBlob helper removes duplicate streaming and hash-classification logic without an actionable style defect.
PILOT-001-R4-001 is untested because all candidate-retention fixtures contain only one implementation round.

findings.expectedBehavior: Every frozen RED test from every implementation round exists unchanged in the final reviewed candidate.
findings.observedBehavior: Each RED blob is compared only with its own intermediate result candidate, so a later candidate may delete, replace, or weaken an earlier regression.
findings.reproduction: Create two valid rounds, preserve round-one RED in candidate one, then delete or replace it in candidate two; validation checks only candidate one for the round-one blob.
findings.impact: A final candidate can discard a regression that justified an earlier production change while retaining apparently valid TDD evidence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Compare every historical frozen RED blob with the final state candidate as well as its round lineage and reject missing, changed, or weakened evidence.
findings.verification: Add genuine two-round Git fixtures whose final candidate preserves, deletes, replaces, and skips the earlier frozen test.

findings.expectedBehavior: Untrusted ticket evidence has deterministic aggregate bounds on Git subprocesses and bytes in addition to the one-megabyte per-file cap.
findings.observedBehavior: The validator permits an unbounded maxRounds value and unbounded testFiles arrays, applying the blob cap separately to every RED and candidate read.
findings.reproduction: Construct many rounds containing many distinct near-limit test blobs; validation can launch tens of thousands of Git subprocesses and read gigabytes before completion.
findings.impact: A repository ticket packet can consume excessive CPU, I/O, and time during a mandatory local or CI validation gate.
findings.requiredRemediation: Enforce a small aggregate test-reference limit and a deterministic total Git blob-byte budget before or during evidence reads, with one stable diagnostic for each bound.
findings.verification: Add boundary and over-budget fixtures for aggregate test references and total RED/final-candidate blob bytes while preserving valid near-limit evidence.

notes: The pre-existing round-one and round-two frozen-test violations are orchestrator-owned bootstrap history and are not misattributed to the round-four candidate diff.
